collection.title: The Stats dictionary of 26 Aug 2026, ported

entry.boundaries: Direction is a property of price structure, not of any single indicator; an oscillator reading or a moving-average slope is a *proxy* for it. Do not confuse trend-direction with momentum strength — a market can trend down while a momentum oscillator rises on a pullback.
entry.definition: The dominant direction of price travel over a chosen lookback, usually expressed as up / down / sideways and identified from a sequence of rising or falling swing highs and lows.
entry.recognition: Compare consecutive swing highs and lows. A sequence of higher highs and higher lows is an uptrend; lower lows and lower highs a downtrend; interleaved/equal pivots a sideways or ranging state. Trendlines and moving-average slope are common shortcuts but must be labelled as proxies, not the definition.

sources.quote: trend, directional bias, higher-high/lower-low structure, market bias
OHLC price series; swing-high/swing-low pivots; optionally a moving average or trendline overlay.
lookback (number of swings or bars) — `unresolved`; pivot-detection strength (e.g. fractal left/right count 2–5) — `published-convention`; minimum bar count for a valid swing sequence — `inferred`.
context, pre-trigger filter (trade only with trend), confirmation (resumption), invalidation (structure break), exit trigger (trend reversal).
Timeframe-relative: a "trend" on M5 may be noise on D1. Requires a decision on which timeframe defines the bias. Works on any OHLC venue (forex and crypto spot included) without special data.
Fully transferable between forex spot and crypto spot; no venue-specific data needed. Futures/equity trend *definitions* transfer, but their session/halt gaps do not.

`ontology-seed — needs source evidence` for a single canonical algorithm; the higher-high/lower-low formulation is widely documented in technical-analysis textbooks (e.g. Dow Theory) but no single URL was fixed this wave.

"Bias" sometimes means a multi-timeframe conclusion, not one-timeframe direction; "structural bias" (ICT/SMC) adds liquidity-sweep context. Pivot-detection thresholds are discretionary and vary by tool.

entry.boundaries: Strength is not direction: the ADX line rises whether the trend is up or down. Not the same as momentum (speed of change) nor volatility (size of range) — a market can be volatile but non-trending (low ADX, high ATR).
entry.definition: A measure of how strongly directional (vs. flat) price movement is over a lookback, independent of the trend's sign.
entry.recognition: ADX is the canonical proxy. Rising ADX = strengthening trend; falling ADX = weakening/flattening. Threshold conventions (below ~20 = no trend; above ~25 = strong) are published rules of thumb, not universal laws.

sources.quote: trend quality, directional strength, ADX level
OHLC series feeding an ADX-type calculation, or a trend-strength statistic.
ADX period 14 — `source-stated` (Wilder default); no-trend threshold 20 and strong-trend threshold 25 — `published-convention`; smoothing method (Wilder's) — `source-stated`.
pre-trigger filter (require a minimum strength before acting), confirmation, regime classifier, exit signal (strength exhaustion).
Lagging and smooth; weak at catching very short scalping turns. Same formula applies across forex and crypto spot.
ADX originates in Wilder's 1978 work for commodities; transfers directly to forex/crypto spot as a price-only statistic with no venue dependency.
Wilder, *New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems* (1978); Investopedia DMI article https://www.investopedia.com/articles/technical/02/050602.asp
Thresholds vary (some use 15/20, some 20/25); `+DI`/`-DI` crossings are a separate directional signal frequently conflated with ADX strength.

entry.boundaries: This is a *coordination* primitive (one timeframe conditioning another), not a new kind of trend. It is not a trigger by itself; it narrows the set of acceptable lower-timeframe triggers.
entry.definition: The trend-direction and/or regime read from a timeframe longer than the entry timeframe, used to constrain which setups are eligible on the lower timeframe.
entry.recognition: Evaluate a trend primitive (e.g. trend-direction, moving-average-trend, structure) on the higher timeframe and require agreement with the intended lower-timeframe trade direction. Disagreement marks the setup as counter-trend and typically excluded or down-weighted.

sources.quote: HTF bias, top-down bias, directional context
Two or more OHLC series (higher + lower timeframe), or a single series resampled to the higher timeframe.
higher-to-lower timeframe ratio (e.g. D1→H1→M15, or H4→M15) — `inferred`, strategy-specific; bias source (structure vs. MA vs. oscillator) — `unresolved`.
pre-trigger filter, context, confluence weight, invalidation (HTF bias flips).
Requires multi-timeframe data for the same instrument; in crypto spot, higher timeframes are continuous (24/7) whereas forex higher timeframes inherit session-based weekly gaps.
Universally applicable across forex and crypto spot; the *method* transfers, the *specific timeframe ladder* is a strategy decision.
`ontology-seed — needs source evidence`; multi-timeframe analysis is standard practice but no single canonical URL was fixed.
Whether "bias" is binary (with/against) or graded (strong/moderate/weak) is unresolved; ratio of timeframes is discretionary.

entry.boundaries: Regime is broader than trend-direction: a range has no direction but is a distinct regime. Regime is a *classification of conditions*, not a specific tradeable event. Do not confuse a regime label with a live directional prediction.
entry.definition: A categorical classification of the current market state — commonly trending, ranging/consolidating, breakout, or high-volatility — intended to select which strategy families are appropriate.
entry.recognition: Combine signals: ADX below threshold + narrow bands ⇒ ranging; ADX above threshold + directional structure ⇒ trending; band/range breakout ⇒ breakout. Regime detection is explicitly multi-indicator and heuristic; there is no single authoritative algorithm.

sources.quote: regime, market state, trending vs. ranging, choppiness regime
OHLC; volatility and trend-strength statistics (ATR, ADX); optionally range-detection (e.g. Donchian width, Bollinger width, ADR percentile).
thresholds for "narrow/wide" (band-width percentile, ATR percentile) — `unresolved`/`inferred`; classification scheme (2/3/4-state) — `unresolved`.
context, pre-trigger filter (mean-reversion vs. trend-following gate), regime switch as invalidation.
Regime is timeframe-dependent (a range on M5 can be a trend on H1). Crypto spot and forex spot both support it from OHLC alone.
Fully transferable; no centralized-exchange data required. Regime *switching* frequency differs across markets but the primitive is market-agnostic.
`ontology-seed — needs source evidence`; the trending/range dichotomy is textbook, but a canonical regime taxonomy is not standardized.
Many named variants (e.g. "quiet/volatile", "breakout/trend/range"); exact state boundaries are discretionary.

entry.boundaries: A moving average is a lagging *smoothing* of price, not a direct structural measurement; it is a trend proxy. Distinct from moving-average-crossover (which needs two averages).
entry.definition: Use of a moving average (typically a longer-period SMA/EMA) as a reference for trend: price above and MA rising = up, price below and MA falling = down.
entry.recognition: Compute the MA. Trend is up when close is above a rising MA and down when close is below a falling MA. The slope and price-relative-to-MA conditions are often combined.

sources.quote: MA trend, price-above-MA, moving-average slope
OHLC series; one moving-average line.
MA type (SMA/EMA/WMA) — `published-convention` (EMA common for intraday); period — strategy-specific `inferred` (common references: 20, 50, 200); slope lookback — `unresolved`.
context, pre-trigger filter (price on correct side), dynamic support/resistance reference, trailing-exit reference.
Price-only; no venue restriction. Lag increases with period; poorly suited to very fast scalping as a standalone.
Directly transferable to forex and crypto spot. Longer periods (e.g. 200) that reference equity calendars transfer only as *bar counts*, not as calendar meaning.
`published-convention` — moving averages are core technical-analysis material; see e.g. StockCharts ChartSchool moving-average entries. No single URL fixed this wave.
EMA vs. SMA vs. WMA choice is discretionary; "above a rising MA" vs. "MA slope only" are competing definitions.

entry.boundaries: The crossover is a *lagging event* that often fires after much of the move is done; it is a regime confirmation, not an early trigger. Not the same as price crossing a single MA.
entry.definition: A transition event where a shorter-period moving average crosses a longer-period moving average, read as a trend-regime change (up-cross = golden cross; down-cross = death cross).
entry.recognition: Compute fast and slow MAs. Crossover occurs when fast crosses above (golden) or below (death) slow. Directional confirmation depends on slope/alignment; in choppy markets crossovers whipsaw.

sources.quote: golden cross / death cross, MA cross, dual-MA signal
OHLC series; two moving averages of different periods.
fast/slow periods — `published-convention` for 50/200 (daily equities) but `unresolved` for intraday crypto/forex; MA type SMA/EMA — `published-convention`.
confirmation (post-trigger regime confirmation), pre-trigger filter, trend-following trigger, exit signal.
Price-only. The 50/200 daily convention is an equity-index legacy; its meaning does not automatically carry to forex/crypto spot without re-parameterization.
The *operation* transfers; the *parameters* must be re-derived per market/timeframe and are not portable defaults.

Investopedia golden/death cross https://www.investopedia.com/ask/answers/121114/what-difference-between-golden-cross-and-death-cross-pattern.asp ; CMC Markets golden/death cross explainer https://www.cmcmarkets.com/en-gb/technical-analysis/golden-cross-and-death-cross-explained
"Golden/death cross" strictly means the 50/200 daily pair in equity media; generalized crossover means any fast/slow pair. Lag is a documented limitation.

entry.boundaries: A structure break is a *discrete event* on swing geometry, distinct from an indicator crossover and from a mere wick poke (whether a break counts on close vs. intrabar is a binding decision). Not an order; it is an observable transition.
entry.definition: A decisive price break of a prior swing high (in an uptrend) or swing low (in a downtrend), used to confirm continuation or signal a potential reversal of market structure.
entry.recognition: In an uptrend, price closing above the most recent swing high = bullish break; in a downtrend, closing below the most recent swing low = bearish break. CHoCH is the first counter-trend break against the prevailing structure.

sources.quote: break of structure (BOS), change of character (CHoCH), swing break, structure shift
OHLC series; swing-high/low pivots.
close-based vs. intrabar confirmation — `unresolved` (strategy-specific); swing-pivot strength — `inferred`; whether a CHoCH or only a BOS is used — `unresolved`.
trigger (breakout entry), confirmation (post-trigger), invalidation (opposing structure break), exit.
Price-only; timeframe-relative. Works identically in forex and crypto spot.
Fully transferable. ICT/SMC vocabulary (BOS/CHoCH) originates in retail futures/forex commentary but the geometry is venue-independent.
`ontology-seed — needs source evidence`; terminology is SMC/ICT-standard but is largely a re-labelling of classical Dow-theory structure.
BOS vs. CHoCH boundary; intrabar vs. close confirmation; whether wick or body defines the swing extreme. All unresolved.

entry.boundaries: A range is not a trend and not a single consolidation pattern; it is a *condition*. Distinct from a breakout (the moment the range is resolved). Chop can coexist with high volatility — ranging does not imply calm.
entry.definition: A market state where price oscillates within a horizontal band without a persistent directional swing structure, so trend-following logic is weak.
entry.recognition: Low ADX with bounded price between recent swing extremes; band width narrow/stable; no new highs/lows over N bars. Heuristic, multi-signal.

sources.quote: sideways market, consolidation, ranging, chop, no-trend state
OHLC; band/range detection (Donchian, Bollinger width, ADR percentile, ADX).
bars without a new high/low — `unresolved`; ADX threshold — `published-convention` (~<20/25); band-width percentile — `inferred`.
pre-trigger filter (suppress trend strategies, enable mean-reversion), context, invalidation (range resolves into trend).
Timeframe-relative. Crypto spot ranges are continuous; forex spot ranges inherit session pauses.
Fully transferable; price/volatility only.
`ontology-seed — needs source evidence`.
"Range" vs. "chop" vs. "distribution/accumulation" terminology is inconsistent across sources.

entry.boundaries: Momentum is about *speed of change*, not direction persistence (trend) nor range size (volatility). The raw MTM indicator is distinct from its normalized relatives (ROC, RSI, MACD).
entry.definition: A measure of the rate/speed of price change over a lookback; the base indicator is the difference between the current price and the price N periods ago.
entry.recognition: MTM = close(t) − close(t−N). Positive = upward momentum, negative = downward; zero-line crossings mark momentum sign changes; magnitude indicates strength.

sources.quote: MTM, momentum indicator, price velocity
OHLC series (closing prices).
lookback N (14 common) — `published-convention`; price field (close) — `published-convention`.
confirmation, trigger (zero-line cross), divergence source, filter.
Price-only; no venue restriction. Unit-bound (in price terms), so not comparable across instruments — use ROC for that.
Directly transferable to forex/crypto spot.
Wikipedia momentum/ROC https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Momentum_(technical_analysis) ; Investopedia ROC https://www.investopedia.com/terms/p/pricerateofchange.asp
MTM vs. ROC are frequently conflated; some platforms label ROC as "momentum".

entry.boundaries: ROC is momentum expressed as a percentage; the raw momentum (MTM) is the absolute difference. Do not treat ROC as a bounded oscillator — it is unbounded and has no fixed overbought/oversold band.
entry.definition: The percentage change of price over a lookback, normalizing momentum so values are comparable across instruments and timeframes.
entry.recognition: ROC = (close(t) − close(t−N)) / close(t−N) × 100. Positive/negative around a zero line; zero-crossings and divergences are the standard readings.

sources.quote: ROC, price rate of change
OHLC series (closing prices).
lookback N (e.g. 10–14) — `published-convention`; price field close — `published-convention`.
confirmation, divergence source, filter, trigger.
Price-only; venue-agnostic.
Directly transferable; percentage form makes cross-market comparison possible.
Investopedia ROC https://www.investopedia.com/terms/p/pricerateofchange.asp
Overbought/oversold "levels" (e.g. ±30%) are arbitrary conventions, not intrinsic.

entry.boundaries: RSI is bounded and normalized (unlike ROC). It measures momentum, not trend. Overbought/oversold readings do not mean "sell/buy now" — in strong trends RSI can stay extreme for extended periods.
entry.definition: A bounded momentum oscillator (0–100) comparing average gains to average losses over a lookback, used to flag overbought/oversold conditions and momentum divergences.
entry.recognition: RSI = 100 − 100/(1+RS), RS = average gain / average loss over N periods. Convention: >70 overbought, <30 oversold. Divergence (price extreme not confirmed by RSI) is a widely cited reversal signal.

sources.quote: Relative Strength Index, Wilder's RSI
OHLC series (closing prices).
period 14 — `source-stated` (Wilder); overbought 70 / oversold 30 — `published-convention` (Wilder's own thresholds); smoothing method — `source-stated`.
filter, confirmation, divergence source, trigger (threshold cross / centerline cross).
Price-only; venue-agnostic. Oscillator, so best-behaved in ranges; threshold reading is regime-dependent.
Originates in Wilder's 1978 commodities work; transfers directly to forex/crypto spot.

Wilder, *New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems* (1978); StockCharts RSI https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/technical-indicators-and-overlays/technical-indicators/relative-strength-index-rsi
Thresholds 70/30 are convention (some use 80/20 in strong trends); "failure swing" vs. "divergence" terminology varies.

entry.boundaries: MACD is a *trend-following, lagging* momentum tool — it confirms moves, it does not forecast them. Distinct from RSI (bounded, gain/loss ratio) and from raw momentum/ROC.
entry.definition: A trend-following momentum indicator built from the difference between two EMAs (the MACD line) plus a signal line (its EMA) and a histogram of their difference.
entry.recognition: MACD line = EMA(fast) − EMA(slow); signal line = EMA(MACD line); histogram = MACD line − signal. Crossovers, zero-line crossings, and divergences are the canonical readings.

sources.quote: Moving Average Convergence Divergence
OHLC series (closing prices).
fast 12 / slow 26 / signal 9 — `source-stated` (Gerald Appel's defaults); EMA type — `published-convention`.
confirmation, trigger (crossover), divergence source, filter, exit.
Price-only; venue-agnostic. Default 12/26/9 assumes a specific bar cadence; intraday re-parameterization is normal.
Originates in equities (Appel); transfers directly to forex/crypto spot as a price-only statistic.
Investopedia MACD https://www.investopedia.com/terms/m/macd.asp ; Wikipedia MACD https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MACD
"Divergence" is an overloaded term (MACD-line-vs-signal divergence vs. price-vs-MACD divergence); histogram-vs-crossover signal conventions differ.

entry.boundaries: Stochastic is a *position-in-range* measure, not a trend or velocity measure. Its overbought/oversold bands (80/20) are convention. Distinct from RSI, which uses gain/loss ratios rather than range position.
entry.definition: A bounded momentum oscillator comparing the current close to its recent high–low range, used for overbought/oversold reads and (per its author) primarily for divergence.
entry.recognition: %K = (close − lowest low(N)) / (highest high(N) − lowest low(N)) × 100; %D = smoothed %K. Crossovers and divergence are the primary signals.

sources.quote: Stochastic, %K/%D, Lane's stochastic
OHLC series.
%K period (14 fast / 5 fast) and %D smoothing (3) — `published-convention`; slow-stochastic variant applies further smoothing — `published-convention`; thresholds 80/20 — `published-convention`.
confirmation, divergence source, filter, trigger.
Price-only; venue-agnostic. Regime-sensitive: extremes persist in trends.
Originates in George Lane's 1950s work; transfers directly to forex/crypto spot.
Wikipedia stochastic oscillator https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stochastic_oscillator
Fast vs. slow vs. full stochastic are distinct variants; Lane emphasized divergence over threshold trading, which is often lost in popularized accounts.

entry.boundaries: Divergence is a *relationship between price and an oscillator*, not the oscillator itself. It is a discretionary/interpretive signal, not an algorithm with one universal form. Bullish (price lower low, oscillator higher low) vs. bearish (price higher high, oscillator lower high) must be distinguished.
entry.definition: A condition where price makes a new extreme but a momentum oscillator fails to confirm it, read as weakening momentum behind the move.
entry.recognition: Align price swing extremes with oscillator swing extremes over the same window; a non-confirming oscillator extreme is the divergence. Requires a defined swing-detection rule to be reproducible.

sources.quote: divergence, RSI divergence, MACD divergence, oscillator divergence
OHLC series; a momentum oscillator (RSI/MACD/stochastic).
oscillator choice — `unresolved`; swing-detection strength — `inferred`; lookback window — `unresolved`.
confirmation (post-trigger), pre-trigger filter, reversal trigger, exit warning.
Price-only; venue-agnostic. Divergence can persist through long trends, so it is unreliable as a standalone timing tool.
Fully transferable; no venue-specific data.
`published-convention`; documented for RSI/MACD/stochastic at StockCharts/Investopedia. No single URL fixed.
Hidden vs. regular divergence; whether wicks or closes define extremes; how many bars constitute a "new extreme" are all unresolved.

entry.boundaries: ATR measures volatility, not trend direction or momentum. It is a magnitude, expressed in price units (or pips), and carries no sign.
entry.definition: A smoothed measure of per-period price range (accounting for gaps via true range), used to quantify volatility and to size stops/targets in price terms.
entry.recognition: TR = max(high−low, |high−prev close|, |low−prev close|); ATR = smoothed mean of TR (Wilder's smoothing). Higher ATR = more volatile; used for volatility-scaled distances (e.g. stops at k×ATR).

sources.quote: ATR, Wilder's volatility
OHLC series.
period 14 — `source-stated` (Wilder); smoothing — `source-stated`; multiplier k for stop distance (e.g. 1.5–3) — `inferred`/strategy-specific.
context (volatility regime), filter (minimum/maximum volatility), parameter base for stops/targets, distance normalizer.
Price-only; venue-agnostic. ATR is absolute per instrument — not comparable across pairs without normalization (e.g. ATR%).
Originates in Wilder's commodities work; transfers directly to forex/crypto spot. In forex, ATR is often quoted in pips.
Investopedia ATR https://www.investopedia.com/terms/a/atr.asp ; Wilder, *New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems* (1978).
Wilder smoothing vs. simple vs. EMA of TR; ATR% normalization is a common but non-standard variant.

entry.boundaries: Bands measure *relative* price position and volatility, not trend direction. Not a standalone signal; Bollinger himself frames them as a context tool to combine with other signals. Distinct from ATR (no mean-reversion centerline) and from Keltner (ATR-based).
entry.definition: A price envelope of a moving average ± k standard deviations, expanding with volatility and contracting when it falls; used for relative-high/low reads and volatility-regime detection.
entry.recognition: Middle = SMA(N); upper/lower = middle ± k×stdev(N). Band width proxies volatility (squeeze = low vol); price touching/exceeding bands marks relative extremes.

sources.quote: Bollinger Bands, BB, volatility bands
OHLC series (closing prices).
period 20 and k 2.0 — `source-stated` (Bollinger's defaults); longer-term profile 50 / 2.5 — `published-convention`.
context (volatility regime / squeeze), filter, confirmation, mean-reversion trigger at bands.
Price-only; venue-agnostic. Assumes roughly stationary volatility; breaks down across extreme regime shifts.
Originates in equities (Bollinger, 1980s); transfers directly to forex/crypto spot.

Fidelity Bollinger Bands https://www.fidelity.com/learning-center/trading-investing/technical-analysis/technical-indicator-guide/bollinger-bands ; TradingView BB https://www.tradingview.com/support/solutions/43000501840-bollinger-bands-bb
%B and bandwidth are derived metrics frequently bundled under "Bollinger" and should be listed as separate primitives if used.

entry.boundaries: Realized/historical volatility is *backward-looking*; it must not be confused with implied volatility (forward-looking, from options) or with ATR (a price-range average, not a return dispersion).
entry.definition: The actual variability of past returns, usually the annualized standard deviation of (log) returns over a lookback.
entry.recognition: Compute returns over a window; take their standard deviation; annualize (×√252 or venue-appropriate). Higher = more volatile. Used as a baseline against forward-looking measures and for regime detection.

sources.quote: historical volatility, statistical volatility, HV, RV
Price series (closes or returns).
lookback (10/20/30/60/252) — `published-convention`; annualization factor — `published-convention` (equity) but `unresolved` for 24/7 crypto; log vs. simple returns — `published-convention`.
context (volatility regime), filter, baseline for implied-vs-realized comparison.
Requires return history; no special venue data. In spot FX/crypto there is no options-implied analog unless a separate options market is available (crypto has options; spot FX IV is usually absent).
Transferable, but the annualization convention and whether "historical" = "realized" naming differ by source.
Investopedia implied vs. historical volatility https://www.investopedia.com/articles/investing-strategy/071616/implied-vs-historical-volatility-main-differences.asp
"Historical" vs. "realized" are used interchangeably by some and distinguished (realized = intraday/high-frequency) by others.

entry.boundaries: IV is *forward-looking* and options-derived, unlike realized volatility (past) or ATR (price range). It is a *sentiment/expectation* measure, not an observed price statistic. In spot FX there is usually no IV; the VIX is an equity index IV proxy, not a currency measure.
entry.definition: The market's forward-looking volatility expectation, backed out from option prices (e.g. solving Black–Scholes for the volatility input).
entry.recognition: Solve an options-pricing model for the volatility consistent with observed option prices. High IV = market expects turbulence; low IV = calm. VIX expresses this for the S&P 500.

sources.quote: IV, expected volatility, option-implied volatility
Options prices (or an IV index like VIX/DVOL); otherwise unavailable.
pricing model (Black–Scholes) — `published-convention`; maturity window (VIX ≈ 30-day) — `published-convention`.
intermarket/risk context, filter (risk-on/off), volatility-regime input.
Only exists where a liquid options market exists. Not available for spot FX directly; available for crypto via options/derivatives (e.g. DVOL). Not available from pure spot OHLC.
As a *risk-regime* signal it transfers to forex/crypto spot only as a correlated external input, and only where such data exists — must be labelled as intermarket, not native.

Investopedia VIX https://www.investopedia.com/terms/v/vix.asp ; Investopedia IV vs HV https://www.investopedia.com/articles/investing-strategy/071616/implied-vs-historical-volatility-main-differences.asp
VIX is equity-specific; crypto IV indices (DVOL) are separate; FX "volatility" typically refers to realized measures or broker-quoted FX options, not a clean IV index.

entry.boundaries: Donchian is *price-extreme*-based (rigid, step-like), unlike Keltner (ATR-based) or Bollinger (stdev-based). It signals new N-period highs/lows, not volatility directly.
entry.definition: A channel drawn from the highest high and lowest low over N periods, used to detect breakouts and to bound ranges.
entry.recognition: Upper = max high(N), lower = min low(N), mid = average. A close above the upper band = new N-bar high (breakout); price within channel = range.

sources.quote: Donchian channel, price channel, N-bar high/low channel
OHLC series.
period N (20 common; 55 for the turtle-trading 20/55 dual system) — `published-convention`.
trigger (breakout), filter, context (range definition), trailing stop reference.
Price-only; venue-agnostic.
Originates in futures trend-following (Richard Donchian / turtle traders); transfers directly to forex/crypto spot.
`published-convention`; Donchian channel is widely documented (e.g. Investopedia bands/channels article https://www.investopedia.com/articles/forex/06/bandschannels.asp).
Single vs. dual-channel (20/55) systems; whether breakout is close-based or intrabar.

entry.boundaries: Keltner uses ATR (volatility) for band width, unlike Bollinger (stdev) or Donchian (price extremes). It is a *trend + volatility* overlay, not a breakout detector per se.
entry.definition: A volatility band around an EMA where band width is a multiple of ATR, used for trend framing and volatility-aware support/resistance.
entry.recognition: Middle = EMA(N); upper/lower = middle ± k×ATR(M). Bands widen/contract with ATR; price position between bands frames trend health.

sources.quote: Keltner channel, ATR channel
OHLC series.
EMA period 20, ATR period 10–20, multiplier k 2 — `published-convention` (values vary by source).
context (trend/volatility framing), filter, confirmation, dynamic stop/target reference.
Price-only; venue-agnostic.
Originates in commodity futures (Chester Keltner, 1960s); transfers directly to forex/crypto spot.
`published-convention`; see Investopedia bands/channels https://www.investopedia.com/articles/forex/06/bandschannels.asp and Keltner-vs-Donchian comparisons.
Parameter conventions differ by platform; some variants use SMA middle line.

entry.boundaries: ADR is a *calendared* average range, distinct from ATR (per-bar, gap-adjusted) and from realized volatility (return dispersion). ADR is session-based and so inherits session boundaries.
entry.definition: The average high−low range over a recent window of days (or sessions), used to judge whether a move or a target distance is "normal" for the instrument.
entry.recognition: ADR = mean(high−low) over N days. Compare current range or a proposed stop/target distance to ADR (and to intraday range elapsed vs. ADR) to gauge room remaining.

sources.quote: ADR, daily range, ADR%
Daily OHLC series.
lookback N (5–20 days) — `inferred`; percent-of-ADR thresholds — `unresolved`.
context (volatility expectation), filter (distance-to-target feasibility), stop/target sanity check.
Needs a defined "day"; forex "day" is broker/server-defined (usually NY close), crypto "day" is usually UTC. This is a session-boundary dependency.
Transferable, but the "day" boundary convention differs between forex (NY close) and crypto (UTC), which changes ADR values.
`ontology-seed — needs source evidence`; ADR is a widely used retail concept without a single canonical citation.
Day-boundary convention; N-bar window; whether to use body-only or full range.

entry.boundaries: This entry is the *family/operation*, not any specific trend reading. A moving average alone is not a signal; it becomes one only when bound (cross, slope, price-relative). Distinct from oscillators and bands.
entry.definition: An indicator family that smooths a price series into a lagged trend line by averaging past values; SMA, EMA, WMA, and HMA are the common members.
entry.recognition: Compute the chosen average over N periods. SMA weights all equally; EMA weights recent bars more. Member choice changes lag and responsiveness.

sources.quote: MA, SMA, EMA, WMA, HMA
OHLC series.
type (SMA/EMA/WMA/HMA) — `published-convention`; period N — strategy-specific `inferred`.
context, filter, dynamic level, component of other primitives (MACD, Bollinger, Keltner).

A source may permit partial entry, require all-or-none, or cancel/hedge residual exposure; each is distinct.

entry.boundaries: Not re-entry after a completed trade, and not automatic permission to chase price indefinitely.
entry.definition: A source-defined attempt to submit a replacement entry order after rejection, cancellation, expiry, or insufficient fill of an earlier attempt.
entry.recognition: Permit a new order only when the prior outcome matches the named retry condition and all original/prioritized setup validity checks remain true.

sources.quote: retry entry; requote; chase retry
Prior order outcome, current signal/setup state, current market data, retry count, and clock.
eligible outcomes, maximum attempts, delay/reprice rule, and cancellation condition — every numerical value `source-stated` or `unresolved`.
execution management; entry lifecycle.
Rejection codes and requote behavior are broker/venue-specific; rapid retry requires latency-aware timestamps.
A decentralized OTC dealer quote/requote process is not equivalent to a rejected CLOB post-only order.
ontology-seed — needs source evidence.
Retrying the same price, repricing to current market, and abandoning after a missed trade are separate policies.

entry.boundaries: Not signal cancellation without an actual order, and not expiry; cancellation has acknowledgement/race semantics.
entry.definition: An operation that requests withdrawal of a still-active, unfilled or partially unfilled entry order.
entry.recognition: Submit cancel when the named condition occurs; continue reconciling fills until the venue confirms final order state, because fills can race with cancellation.

sources.quote: cancel unfilled order; withdraw entry order
Order identifier/status, fills, cancellation request/acknowledgement, linked signal state, and current exposure.
cancellation condition, affected order scope, residual-fill policy, and linked-order action — all `source-stated` or `unresolved`.
execution management; signal cancellation; risk control.
An accepted cancellation request does not retroactively prevent a fill that matched first.
Futures/CLOB status progression is exchange-specific; OTC-FX pending instructions are broker/dealer-specific.
CME notes that a resting limit remains until executed, canceled, or expires: https://www.cmegroup.com/education/courses/things-to-know-before-trading-cme-futures/futures-order-types
Cancel-on-invalidation, cancel-on-session-end, and cancel-on-opposite-signal are separate triggers.

entry.boundaries: Not position time stop; not discretionary cancellation. It occurs before full entry.
entry.definition: Automatic loss of eligibility of an unfilled order or armed entry opportunity at a designated time/event.
entry.recognition: At the specified deadline or state boundary, mark the signal/order expired and request/corroborate cancellation if the venue has not already expired it.

sources.quote: entry timeout; order timeout; signal expiry
Order/signal activation time, expiry rule, venue time-in-force, calendar/session state, and order status.
expiry timestamp/duration/bar count/session endpoint, timezone, and action after expiry — all values `source-stated` or `unresolved`.
entry lifecycle; signal cancellation; timing constraint.
Native time-in-force and strategy-level signal expiry can disagree; represent both when relevant.

Coinbase documents GTC, GTT, and IOC options for its limit orders. These labels and availability must not be presumed for an FX broker. https://help.coinbase.com/coinbase/trading-and-funding/advanced-trade/order-types
cited venue documentation.
“Valid for one candle” needs a declared start/end and bar source.

entry.boundaries: Not the strategy's setup expiry, although it can implement part of one; availability and exact semantics are venue-specific.
entry.definition: A venue/order instruction defining how long an order may remain active and, for some forms, whether immediate full or partial execution is acceptable.
entry.recognition: Preserve the explicit time-in-force submitted with each order and evaluate results according to that venue's defined behavior rather than generic label assumptions.

sources.quote: TIF; GTC; GTT; IOC; FOK
Order instruction, acknowledgement, fill quantity, cancellation/expiry status, and venue rulebook.
instruction label and deadline where applicable — `source-stated`; unsupported label — `unresolved`.
execution constraint; pending-order lifecycle.
GTC may be subject to venue cancellation rules, maintenance, or product lifecycle; IOC permits partial execution by definition on many venues.

Coinbase defines GTC, GTT, and IOC for its Advanced orders; CME/order-routing firms may expose a broader/different set. https://help.coinbase.com/coinbase/trading-and-funding/advanced-trade/order-types
cited venue documentation.
Fill-or-kill must not be inferred from IOC; it requires its own venue-supported semantics.

entry.boundaries: Not an order type and not a cooldown; it specifies consumption and reset semantics.
entry.definition: A state rule limiting a recognized setup to one defined entry attempt, fill, or completed trade before reset.
entry.recognition: Create a durable instance when setup arms; after the specified consuming event, suppress further entries from that instance until a separately defined reset/rearm occurs.

sources.quote: single-use signal; consume-on-attempt; no-repeat entry
Setup instance identity, order attempts/fills, trade lifecycle, and reset condition.
consuming event, scope identity, reset event, and treatment of rejected/partial orders — all `source-stated` or `unresolved`.
entry lifecycle; risk control; sequencing.
Requires state continuity across bar/session transitions and reconciliation of rejected/canceled orders.
Portable across markets; venue is relevant only to what counts as a submitted/accepted/filled attempt.
ontology-seed — needs source evidence.
One-shot may mean one order attempt, one fill, or one position per level; do not collapse them.

entry.boundaries: Not expiry of the prior signal and not time stop on an open trade; it gates subsequent entries.
entry.definition: A rule prohibiting new entry attempts for a defined interval or state period after a specified event.
entry.recognition: On the named event, start a lockout timer/state; reject otherwise-valid new entries until the duration ends or reset condition occurs.

sources.quote: lockout; refractory period; wait-after-trade
Triggering event time/state, clock/bar count/session state, candidate signal state, and position state.
triggering event, duration/bar/session rule, scope (instrument/direction/strategy), and override conditions — all values `source-stated` or `unresolved`.
entry filter; re-entry control; management.
Requires a timezone/bar construction and a stable instrument identity.
Portable. Continuous crypto trading makes clock/session selection explicit; futures halts and FX rollovers may interrupt the chosen time basis.
ontology-seed — needs source evidence.
A cooldown after loss, after exit, and after any attempt are distinct rules.

entry.boundaries: Not retry of an unfilled order and not automatic reversal. It begins after a position/trade lifecycle event.
entry.definition: A new entry into the same directional or setup idea after a prior position was reduced or closed.
entry.recognition: Permit a fresh entry only if the re-entry condition, reset/rearm condition, and any maximum-attempt rule are explicitly satisfied; create a new trade instance.

sources.quote: reengagement; second entry; re-open
Prior trade state/outcome, new/continuing setup state, cooldown/one-shot state, current market data, and new order status.
eligible prior exit types, rearm trigger, delay/cooldown, maximum re-entries, order type, and sizing rule — all values `source-stated` or `unresolved`.
entry; execution management; sequencing.
Position accounting must distinguish a re-entry from a partial fill or an order amendment.
Crypto spot re-entry must have quote-currency inventory/balance; futures/OTC margin mechanics may differ materially.
ontology-seed — needs source evidence.
Re-enter at same level, after new confirmation, or on reclaim are separate variants.

entry.boundaries: Not merely listing entry and exit rules together; it requires a defined parent-child state relation.
entry.definition: A rule that activates, sizes, modifies, or cancels a child protective/target order in response to a parent entry order's acknowledgement or fill state.
entry.recognition: On each parent fill event, apply the stated activation threshold and child quantity rule; reconcile child orders as parent fills, is canceled, or is partially filled.

sources.quote: parent-child order; attached TP/SL; conditional child order
Parent order/fills, position quantity, child order statuses, linkage policy, and cancellations.
activation event, quantity basis, linkage/OCO policy, partial-fill rule, and cancellation rule — all `source-stated` or `unresolved`.
execution management; protection; exits.
Atomicity is venue-specific; non-native implementations have race risk between parent fill and child protection placement.

Coinbase says its TP/SL activates when the parent order starts filling and sizes the exit to filled quantity; this is a platform-specific implementation, not a portable guarantee. https://help.coinbase.com/coinbase/trading-and-funding/advanced-trade/order-types
cited venue documentation.
Child activation on partial fill versus full fill changes protection timing materially.

entry.boundaries: Not platform governance, a recommendation, or a guarantee of maximum realized loss; gaps, slippage, costs, and stop non-fill can exceed an estimate.
entry.definition: A source-native sizing concept that chooses position quantity so a stated loss-at-stop estimate corresponds to a stated fraction of an account/equity reference.
entry.recognition: Preserve the source's calculation inputs and sizing instruction; distinguish intended risk at reference prices from realized outcome.

sources.quote: percent-risk sizing; fractional-risk model
Account/equity reference, entry estimate/actual fill, stop reference, contract/lot/instrument value, costs if source includes them.
equity basis, risk fraction, stop basis, instrument value conversion, and cost/slippage treatment — every value `source-stated` or `unresolved`.
sizing input; management; source-native risk claim.
FX pip value depends on pair/account currency and lot; futures have contract multipliers; crypto spot size is base/quote inventory constrained.
The concept transfers only after instrument-value and account-currency conversion are made explicit; no default fraction is standardized here.
ontology-seed — needs source evidence.
Risk may be computed from planned entry versus actual fill, producing different quantities.

entry.boundaries: Not fixed position notional and not a claim of realized-loss certainty.
entry.definition: A source-native sizing concept that targets a stated nominal currency loss estimate at a defined protective-stop reference.
entry.recognition: Determine quantity from the source-stated loss estimate per unit between entry and stop, preserving conversion timing and rounding rules.

sources.quote: fixed-dollar risk; fixed monetary risk
Cash-risk amount, entry/stop estimates, instrument-value conversion, account currency, and costs if included.
cash amount, account currency, entry/stop basis, conversion rate, rounding, and cost treatment — all values `source-stated` or `unresolved`.
sizing input; source-native risk claim.
Cross-currency FX conversion can change risk; futures multiplier and crypto quote denomination must be known.
Do not treat a futures contract dollar-per-tick relationship as a spot-FX pip value or a crypto unit value.
ontology-seed — needs source evidence.
The nominal amount may be fixed per trade, per day, or per setup; scope is essential.

entry.boundaries: Not risk-normalized sizing: the estimated loss at a stop changes when stop distance or instrument price changes.
entry.definition: A source-native sizing instruction using the same stated quantity, lot amount, or quote-currency notional for each qualifying trade.
entry.recognition: Submit the stated quantity after applying venue increment/minimum rules; record any rounding or insufficient-balance outcome.

sources.quote: fixed size; fixed lot; fixed units
Instrument quantity/lot/notional definition, account balance/inventory if relevant, entry price, and lot/minimum increments.
quantity unit, fixed amount, rounding rule, and insufficient-balance action — all values `source-stated` or `unresolved`.
sizing input; source-native risk claim.
“Lot” is broker/instrument-specific; crypto base amount and quote notional are different sizing units.
Futures contract count, OTC-FX lot, and crypto base quantity must not be silently converted into each other.
ontology-seed — needs source evidence.
A fixed quantity can be fixed per instrument or normalized by a source-defined basket; retain scope.

entry.boundaries: Not necessarily fixed-fractional sizing: the target may be a cash amount, a volatility budget, or another source-defined quantity.
entry.definition: A sizing relationship in which planned position quantity changes with the distance between an entry reference and a protective-stop reference.
entry.recognition: Calculate adverse movement per unit between entry and stop and use the stated target risk measure to derive a permissible quantity; preserve treatment of changed stops after entry.

sources.quote: size-from-stop; inverse-stop-distance sizing
Entry reference, stop reference, direction, instrument-value conversion, target risk measure, and rounding/minimums.
entry/stop basis, target risk measure, conversion, rounding, and pre/post-fill recalculation policy — all values `source-stated` or `unresolved`.
sizing input; management; source-native risk claim.
Need a valid unit-value model, including FX quote/account conversion or futures multiplier.
No sizing formula is presumed universal between OTC FX, centralized futures, and crypto spot.
ontology-seed — needs source evidence.
Some sources size at planned stop; others resize after actual fill or do not resize at all.

entry.boundaries: Not partial fill and not re-entry after flat; the original exposure remains open while quantity increases.
entry.definition: A source-defined operation that adds exposure in one or more later tranches after an initial entry.
entry.recognition: When an add trigger occurs, submit the stated additional quantity; update aggregate average entry, total exposure, and all linked protection/target quantities according to the source rule.

sources.quote: add-on entry; pyramid; averaging in; tranche entry
Existing position, add trigger, permitted direction, add quantity, average fill, new protective/target instructions, and account/inventory availability.
add trigger, tranche quantity, maximum tranches, averaging/pyramiding condition, and revised-stop rule — all values `source-stated` or `unresolved`.
management; entry; source-native sizing/risk claim.
Requires clear aggregate versus per-tranche accounting; spot inventory and margin/contract rules constrain feasibility.
“Averaging down” and trend pyramiding have materially different risks but are both staged-entry operations; neither is endorsed by this entry.
ontology-seed — needs source evidence.
Adds can be at better price, worse price, time intervals, or confirmation events.

entry.boundaries: Not a claim that all retail FX brokers operate identically, and not equivalent to a centralized futures exchange or one crypto exchange book.
entry.definition: The execution context in which spot-FX prices, liquidity, and order handling are supplied through specific dealer, broker, or liquidity-provider relationships rather than one universal public central limit order book.
entry.recognition: Attach each execution rule to the named broker/dealer feed and its stated trigger, pending-order, and fill conventions; mark absent venue details `unresolved`.

sources.quote: dealer FX; broker FX; OTC FX market structure
Broker/dealer quote stream, bid/ask, order confirmations, broker order policy, roll/session schedule, and fill reports.
broker/dealer, quote source, order-policy version, server timezone, and account execution model — all `source-stated` or `unresolved`.
market/data constraint; execution provenance; transfer constraint.
BIS characterizes FX and OTC derivatives as OTC markets and reports on their size/structure; the relevant retail feed remains only a partial venue-specific observation.
Centralized futures volume/depth and a crypto exchange order book are not complete observations of OTC FX liquidity.
BIS Triennial Survey overview: https://www.bis.org/statistics/rpfx22.htm ; BIS discussion of less-visible and bilateral FX trading: https://www.bis.org/publ/qtrpdf/r_qt2212d.pdf
ECN, single-dealer, multi-dealer, and retail broker models require source/broker evidence.

entry.boundaries: Not the intended STRATS venue and not interchangeable with spot price trading merely because both show candles.
entry.definition: The execution context of a listed futures contract traded under a specific exchange rulebook, contract specification, tick size, matching engine, and session calendar.
entry.recognition: Retain source contract and exchange identity with any primitive relying on volume, depth, stops, protections, or sessions; state transfer assumptions separately.

sources.quote: exchange-traded futures context; CLOB futures context
Contract symbol/specification, exchange trade/book data, tick size, session state, order acknowledgements/fills, and rulebook/order-type documentation.
contract, exchange, tick value/size, session, order type, and protection mechanism — all `source-stated`, `published-convention`, or `unresolved`.
market/data constraint; source provenance; transfer constraint.
CME specifies futures order types, including exchange-specific stop and protection behavior; these mechanisms arise from that venue's rules.
Futures-derived price action can be researched as source material, but centralized volume/order-book/last-trade claims are not silently transformed into Forex or crypto-spot facts.
CME futures order types: https://www.cmegroup.com/education/courses/things-to-know-before-trading-cme-futures/futures-order-types
A futures source may use continuous contracts, front months, or regular-trading-hours data; each affects recognition.

entry.boundaries: Not crypto derivatives, not a market-wide crypto order book, and not a guarantee that an order feature is available in all regions/pairs.
entry.definition: The execution context of buying or selling actual spot crypto assets on a named exchange market with its own order book, balances, fees, trading rules, and available contingent features.
entry.recognition: Bind execution behavior to exchange and pair, reconcile base/quote balances after every fill, and distinguish a spot sale of held asset from derivative position reduction.

sources.quote: CEX spot context; crypto exchange spot book
Named exchange/pair, order book/trades, balances, tick/size increments, fees, order status, and exchange rules.
exchange, pair, base/quote units, order feature, size/price increments, and balance policy — all `source-stated` or `unresolved`.
market/data constraint; execution provenance; entry/exit constraint.
Order-book/depth data are exchange-local. Spot short exposure commonly requires borrowing/margin facilities outside simple held-inventory selling.
Coinbase's order types and bracket behavior provide one exchange example, not a universal crypto-spot contract. https://help.coinbase.com/coinbase/trading-and-funding/advanced-trade/order-types
cited exchange documentation.
Centralized-exchange spot and DEX spot have different matching, custody, latency, and order semantics.

entry.boundaries: Not a trading signal itself and not a claim that data are useless; it prevents scope inflation.
entry.definition: The constraint that observed trades, displayed depth, volume, and order-flow features describe only their named venue/feed and may not represent the broader market.
entry.recognition: Label every volume/order-book-derived primitive with the exact market/feed it measures and reject transfer claims lacking a stated link to the target market.

sources.quote: venue-local depth; volume provenance; order-flow scope
Data vendor/feed, venue, instrument, timestamp, depth/trade fields, and coverage statement.
venue/feed identity, instrument mapping, depth level, aggregation window, and coverage caveat — all `source-stated` or `unresolved`.
market/data constraint; evidence qualifier; transfer constraint.
Futures and centralized crypto exchange data can be coherent venue data; spot-FX retail volume/depth is commonly broker/feed-specific.
Do not call broker DOM the complete FX order book; do not call one exchange's BTC spot book the complete crypto market.
Consistent with BIS discussion of less-visible and bilateral FX venues: https://www.bis.org/publ/qtrpdf/r_qt2212d.pdf ; ontology-seed for operational labeling.
Aggregated multi-venue data require a disclosed aggregation method and timing alignment.

entry.boundaries: Not strategy logic by itself and not platform governance; it is necessary to tell whether an intended entry/exit/management action actually occurred.
entry.definition: The operation of reconciling intended signals/orders with authoritative acknowledgements, fills, cancellations, and current actual exposure.
entry.recognition: Treat broker/exchange execution reports and actual exposure as authoritative for state; update strategy instance state only after defined events and retain unknown/inconsistent states visibly.

sources.quote: execution reconciliation; fill-state audit; order state machine
Order identifiers, timestamps, acknowledgements, rejects, fills, cancellations, positions/inventory, and linked-order states.
authoritative source, reconciliation cadence, linkage identifiers, and unresolved-state handling — all `source-stated` or `unresolved`.
execution management; evidence/provenance; risk control.
Order state names and atomicity vary by broker/exchange; a UI/chart marker is not necessarily authoritative execution evidence.
Essential in all target markets, but the concrete reports differ: OTC-FX dealer confirmations, futures exchange reports, and crypto exchange REST/WebSocket order states.
ontology-seed — needs source evidence.
Whether a strategy reacts on acknowledgement, partial fill, full fill, or settled inventory must be explicit.

entry.boundaries: Not an opposing-signal exit alone, and not necessarily an atomic exchange order. It has both an exit and a new-entry leg.
entry.definition: A sequenced operation that closes or reduces an existing exposure and then opens exposure in the opposite direction under explicitly linked conditions.
entry.recognition: Define whether the new leg may submit before the exit fills, only after flat confirmation, or only after an additional confirmation; reconcile partial fills to prevent unintended double exposure.

sources.quote: stop-and-reverse; flip; reverse on signal
Existing position, reversal trigger, exit order/fills, new-entry prerequisites, new-order/fills, and residual exposure.
trigger, exit form, flat-confirmation requirement, new-entry form/size, and failure policy — all `source-stated` or `unresolved`.
exit; entry; management; sequencing.
Atomic reversal functions, reduce-only controls, netting/hedging modes, and shortability differ by venue/account.
Simple crypto spot inventory cannot always create opposite short exposure; futures and margin-enabled OTC FX may support it under different rules.
ontology-seed — needs source evidence.
“Reverse” can mean close then wait, close-and-open immediately, or hedge; do not normalize.

entry.boundaries: More specific than generic cooldown because the lock attaches to an exit category and a requalification policy; not an exit operation itself.
entry.definition: A rule that restricts new entries after a specified exit event until a named requalification, time interval, or market-state reset occurs.
entry.recognition: On a named exit (for example stop-triggered or target-filled), set the scope-specific lock; allow later entry only when the stated reset/rearm condition is met.

sources.quote: stop-out lock; exit lockout; no-chase rule
Exit classification, timestamp, signal/setup instances, reset condition, and position state.
covered exit types, lock scope, reset/requalification condition, and duration if any — all values `source-stated` or `unresolved`.
re-entry control; entry filter; management sequencing.
Depends on trustworthy exit classification and actual fill state, not merely a target/stop touch.
Portable; exact handling of partially exited versus fully flat position must be stated.
ontology-seed — needs source evidence.
Some sources forbid only same-direction re-entry, while others prohibit all new trades in an instrument/session.

entry.boundaries: Not a target reference alone, partial exit alone, or ordinary trailing stop; it explicitly defines a target-event-to-management transition.
entry.definition: A management state transition in which interaction with a target changes the protective-threshold rule for remaining exposure, rather than necessarily closing all exposure.
entry.recognition: When the stated target event occurs, apply the stated partial-exit/remainder rule and initialize or alter the trailing threshold only for the remaining exposure.

sources.quote: trail after TP; runner management; protect after objective
Target-touch/fill event, remaining quantity, existing stop/reference, new trailing-rule inputs, and child-order state.
qualifying target event, retained quantity, new trail type/distance, and order-amendment policy — all values `source-stated` or `unresolved`.
management; exit; trailing protection.
Fill versus touch must be distinguished; order amendments can race with partial fills.
Native linked conditional management is venue-specific; managed implementations require explicit reconciliation.
ontology-seed — needs source evidence.
A source may move to break-even, fixed trail, structure trail, or full close at first target.

entry.boundaries: Not a universal cost model and not a promise of realized net result; it is a source-native reference construction.
entry.definition: A target or break-even reference adjusted by stated transaction costs, spread, financing, or expected execution effects to express a net rather than chart-price objective.
entry.recognition: Apply only the stated cost components and price-side convention when calculating the reference; record unknown costs rather than silently setting them to zero.

sources.quote: net target; cost-adjusted break-even; executable target
Entry fills, bid/ask spread, commission/fees, financing if included, target/stop rule, and account currency conversion.
cost components, estimate source, price basis, account conversion, and update policy — all values `source-stated` or `unresolved`.
target reference; break-even adjustment; sizing input; management.
OTC-FX spread and financing, futures commissions/tick values, and crypto maker/taker fees differ by account and venue.
A source's fixed futures commission/tick calculation cannot be ported directly to spot FX or crypto spot.
ontology-seed — needs source evidence.

“Break-even plus costs” needs the actual cost set and whether slippage is included. - `level-invalidation`, `setup-invalidation`, and `signal-cancellation` are distinct state changes: reference validity, complete setup validity, and an armed unfilled signal respectively. - `stop-reference`, `protective-stop-order`, `target-reference`, `exit-trigger`, and `exit-order` deliberately remain separate. A strategy binding may connect them, but none implies the next. - `partial-exit` is intentional management; `partial-fill-handling` is an execution outcome. `entry-retry` occurs after an unfilled/failed attempt; `re-entry` occurs after a position/trade lifecycle event. - `time-stop`, `pending-order-expiry`, `time-in-force`, and `entry-cooldown` apply to different objects: open position, pending opportunity/order, order instruction, and future-entry permission. - The four exit-status concepts are metadata/status primitives, not trading exits. They preserve source fidelity without designing any external policy. 1. Should source-native sizing concepts remain dictionary primitives or be represented as documented source claims with optional primitive links? 2. Should `deliberately-open`, `external-policy`, `unresolved`, and `source-defined` be dictionary entries, controlled status vocabulary, or both? 3. Is a stop reference that is explicitly used for sizing but never acted on better called a risk reference than a protective stop reference? 4. Which venue-neutral vocabulary should distinguish order acceptance, activation, trigger, matching, partial fill, full fill, cancellation acknowledgement, and settlement/inventory update? 5. How should strategy bindings state a target/stop collision within one OHLC bar when source evidence supplies only bar data? 6. What minimum evidence is required to classify a creator's discretionary “manage the trade” language as `deliberately_open` rather than `unresolved`?

entry.boundaries: Not a "resistance level" (a swing high is a single observed pivot; resistance is an interpretive role/zone). Not the same as a higher high (a swing high is one pivot; "higher high" is a *comparison* between two swing highs). Not a session high (which is time-anchored, not structure-anchored).
entry.definition: A local upper turning point: a bar (or small cluster) whose high is higher than the highs of a fixed number of bars on each side, after which price trades lower.
entry.recognition: For a chosen N, mark bar t as a swing high when `high[t] > high[t±i]` for all `i in 1..N`. Confirmation is inherently lagged by N bars. Wicks vs bodies: most conventions use the high (wick extreme), not the close. No universal N; the same chart yields different pivots at different N.

sources.quote: pivot high, local high, reaction high, fractal high (Bill Williams)
OHLC bar series; a lookback/strength parameter N.

`strength N` — `published-convention` fractal default N=2 (Bill Williams); `source-stated` N=3–5 typical on 5-min futures (dhawal.org); `unresolved` for a STRATS-wide default. `use-wick` vs `use-body` — `unresolved`.
location, trigger (break of a swing high), invalidation (stop reference), context (structure reading), confirmation.
Pure OHLC; no volume needed. Timeframe-dependent — a swing high on M5 is not a swing high on H1. Repainting risk if evaluated intrabar.
Fully transferable to Forex spot and crypto spot (OHLC is universal). No venue-specific dependency.

https://sdk-trading.com/en/price-action/market-structure/swing-highs-and-swing-lows ; https://bharathshiksha.com/articles-html/market-structure-deep-dive.html ; https://dhawal.org/research/futures-ta/chapters/ch02-market-structure.html
Fractal (N=2) vs "significant swing" (ATR-filtered, N=3–5) definitions conflict. Whether confirmation requires a close beyond the pivot or just a wick is discretionary.

entry.boundaries: Not a "support level" (observed pivot vs interpretive role). Not a lower low (single pivot vs comparison). Not a session low (time-anchored).
entry.definition: A local lower turning point: a bar (or small cluster) whose low is lower than the lows of a fixed number of bars on each side, after which price trades higher.
entry.recognition: Mirror of swing-high: mark bar t when `low[t] < low[t±i]` for `i in 1..N`. Same lag and N-sensitivity caveats.

sources.quote: pivot low, local low, reaction low, fractal low
OHLC bar series; lookback/strength N.
`strength N` — `published-convention` N=2 fractal; `source-stated` N=3–5; `unresolved` STRATS default. `use-wick` vs `use-body` — `unresolved`.
location, trigger, invalidation, context, confirmation.
Pure OHLC; timeframe-dependent; intrabar repainting.
Fully transferable to Forex/crypto spot.
https://sdk-trading.com/en/price-action/market-structure/swing-highs-and-swing-lows ; https://bharathshiksha.com/articles-html/market-structure-deep-dive.html
Same fractal-vs-significant-swing conflict as swing-high.

entry.boundaries: This is a *sequence/relationship*, not a single price level. It is the raw material for trend/range classification but is not itself "the trend" (trend is an interpretation). Not to be confused with break-of-structure (a specific violation event).
entry.definition: The ordered comparison of consecutive swing highs and swing lows, read as a sequence. HH = a swing high above the prior swing high; HL = a swing low above the prior swing low; LH = a swing high below the prior swing high; LL = a swing low below the prior swing low.
entry.recognition: After each newly confirmed swing, compare it to the most recent prior swing of the same kind. Uptrend = HH+HL sequence; downtrend = LH+LL; range = mixed/alternating. Minimum length for a trend label is typically two confirmed swings of each kind (four pivots).

sources.quote: HH/HL/LH/LL, market structure, trend structure, swing structure
A confirmed set of swing highs and swing lows (see swing-high/swing-low).
`min-swings-for-trend` — `source-stated` 4 pivots (dhawal.org); `unresolved` STRATS default. Inherits swing `strength N`.
context (regime), filter, confirmation, location (the last HL/LL as a reference).
OHLC only; depends entirely on the swing-detection parameterization; timeframe-dependent.
Fully transferable to Forex/crypto spot.
https://bharathshiksha.com/articles-html/market-structure-deep-dive.html ; https://dhawal.org/research/futures-ta/chapters/ch02-market-structure.html
